title: The Philosophy and Theology of Averroes
author: ibn-rushd
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: Three treatises by Ibn Rushd on the relation between religion and philosophy. The Decisive Discourse argues that the Law commands the study of creation and that demonstrative reasoning cannot contradict it; the Appendix takes up the problem of eternal knowledge; the Exposition of the Methods of Argument examines the doctrines of the faith and the damage done by rival interpretations.
historicalContext: Written in Almohad Spain and Morocco in the late twelfth century, when the public role of philosophy was contested. The Arabic text of the Decisive Discourse was edited by D. H. Muller in 1859; this English translation was published at Baroda in 1921.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1921 translation by Mohammad Jamil-ur-Rehman is public domain in the United States.
